Lagodekhi Protected Areas

Georgia's oldest nature reserve on the Azerbaijani border — forest, waterfalls and the multi-day trek to Black Rock Lake.

Time needed
6 h
From Tbilisi
160 km · 2:40
Road
Paved
Car needed
Economy class
Season
May–October
Entry
free

Lagodekhi was established in 1912 and is the oldest protected area in Georgia. It runs up the southern slope of the Caucasus from the floor of the Alazani Valley to peaks above three thousand metres, and that range of altitude is what gives it its variety: hornbeam and beech forest low down, subalpine meadow higher, then rock and scree at the top. Chamois, bezoar goat, brown bear and red deer all live inside the reserve.

Most routes start from a single base, the visitor centre in Lagodekhi town. The short option is the Gurgeniani waterfall, three to four hours there and back on a well-marked forest path that stays cool even in summer. A step up are the Mashavera falls and the nine-kilometre circular forest trail, both comfortable half-day walks with a solid climb in the middle.

The reserve's headline objective is Black Rock Lake, a glacial lake at around 2,800 metres directly on the Azerbaijani border. The trek takes two or three days with a night at a bivouac site or shelter, and runs from June to October; snow lingers well into May. Registration at the visitor centre is compulsory for every walk, and because the upper route enters a border zone, you must carry your passport for the multi-day trek.

Practical advice

Start at the visitor centre — registration is free and mandatory, and you get a map plus current trail conditions at the same time. Leave the car there. For a day walk, trainers and two litres of water are enough; you will not be sent up to Black Rock Lake without a tent and a passport. Ticks are present in the forest, so covered clothing is sensible. Cafés and ATMs are in the centre of Lagodekhi town.

How to get there from Tbilisi

From Tbilisi take the Kakheti Highway through Sagarejo, Badiauri, Tsnori and Kvareli, then continue east to Lagodekhi — about 160 km and two hours forty. The road is asphalt the whole way and has improved considerably in recent years, so an economy car is entirely adequate. The visitor centre is signposted at the northern edge of town. Fuel and shops are available in Lagodekhi itself. Note that crossing into Azerbaijan is not permitted in a Georgian rental car.

Nearby places

Town

A small walled town on a ridge above the Alazani Valley, with the most photographed view in Kakheti.

Bodbe Monastery

The burial place of St Nino beside Sighnaghi — one of Kakheti's most visited shrines, with a cypress avenue and valley views.

Winery

Kvareli and the Kindzmarauli zone

Kakheti's main red-wine microzone — tunnel cellars cut into rock, two lakes and a natural base for a harvest trip.
